source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם וַיִּקְבְּצ֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים אֶת־מַֽחֲנֵיהֶם֙ לַצָּבָ֔א לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אָכִישׁ֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד יָדֹ֣עַ תֵּדַ֗ע כִּ֤י אִתִּי֙ תֵּצֵ֣א בַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה אַתָּ֖ה וַאֲנָשֶֽׁיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in the days those, and gathered [the] Philistines their camps for the army to fight against Israel; and said Achish to David, Surely you will know that with me you will go out in the camp, you and your men.

en.L: And it came about in those days that the Philistines gathered their camps for war, to fight against Israel. And Achish said to David, "You surely know that you will go out with me in the camp, you and your men."
en.B: In those days the Philistines brought their forces together for war, to fight against Israel. Achish told David, "Understand this clearly: you and your men are going out to battle with me, in my army."
en.R: At that time the Philistines brought all their troops together to go to war against Israel. Achish said to David, "You know, of course, that you and your men will march out with me and my army."

es.L: Y sucedió en aquellos días que los filisteos reunieron sus campamentos para la guerra, para pelear contra Israel. Y dijo Aquis a David: «Sabe bien que saldrás conmigo en el campamento, tú y tus hombres».
es.B: En aquellos días los filisteos juntaron sus fuerzas para la guerra, para pelear contra Israel. Aquis le dijo a David: «Entiende bien esto: tú y tus hombres {{plural_you:saldrán|saldréis}} conmigo a la batalla, en mi ejército».
es.R: En ese tiempo los filisteos reunieron todas sus tropas para ir a la guerra contra Israel. Aquis le dijo a David: «Ya sabes, por supuesto, que tú y tus hombres {{plural_you:saldrán|saldréis}} conmigo y con mi ejército».

fr.L: Et il arriva en ces jours-là que les Philistins rassemblèrent leurs camps pour la guerre, pour combattre contre Israël. Et Akish dit à David : « Tu sais bien que tu sortiras avec moi dans le camp, toi et tes hommes. »
fr.B: En ce temps-là, les Philistins réunirent leurs forces pour faire la guerre à Israël. Akish dit à David : « Sache-le bien : toi et tes hommes, vous partirez au combat avec moi, dans mon armée. »
fr.R: À cette époque, les Philistins ont rassemblé toutes leurs troupes pour faire la guerre contre Israël. Akish a dit à David : « Tu sais, bien sûr, que tes hommes et toi, vous allez partir avec moi et mon armée. »

sw.L: Ikawa siku zile Wafilisti wakakusanya kambi zao kwa vita, ili kupigana na Israeli. Akishi akamwambia Daudi, "Hakika ujue kwamba utatoka pamoja nami kambini, wewe na watu wako."
sw.B: Siku zile Wafilisti wakakusanya majeshi yao kwa vita, ili kupigana na Israeli. Akishi akamwambia Daudi, "Elewa hili waziwazi: wewe na watu wako mtatoka pamoja nami vitani, katika jeshi langu."
sw.R: Wakati huo Wafilisti wakakusanya askari wao wote kwenda kupigana na Israeli. Akishi akamwambia Daudi, "Bila shaka unajua kwamba wewe na watu wako mtakwenda pamoja nami na jeshi langu."

vi.L: Trong những ngày ấy, người Phi-li-tin tập hợp các trại quân của họ để ra trận đánh Y-sơ-ra-ên. A-kích nói với Đa-vít: "Ngươi hẳn biết rằng ngươi sẽ cùng ta ra đi trong trại quân, ngươi và những người của ngươi."
vi.B: Trong thời gian ấy, người Phi-li-tin tập hợp quân lực để gây chiến với Y-sơ-ra-ên. A-kích nói với Đa-vít: "Ngươi phải biết rõ điều này: ngươi và thuộc hạ sẽ cùng ta ra trận, trong đạo quân của ta."
vi.R: Lúc ấy người Phi-li-tin tập hợp tất cả quân lính để đi đánh Y-sơ-ra-ên. A-kích nói với Đa-vít: "Dĩ nhiên ngươi biết là ngươi và thuộc hạ sẽ cùng ta và quân đội của ta ra trận."

ko.L: 그리고 그 무렵에 블레셋 사람들이 이스라엘과 싸우려고 전쟁을 위해 자기들의 진영을 모았다. 그리고 아기스가 다윗에게 말했다. "너와 네 부하들이 나와 함께 진영에 나가야 한다는 것을 너는 분명히 알아라."
ko.B: 그 무렵 블레셋 사람들이 이스라엘과 싸우려고 군대를 모았다. 아기스가 다윗에게 말했다. "분명히 알아 두어라. 너와 네 부하들은 내 군대에 들어 나와 함께 싸우러 나가야 한다."
ko.R: 그 무렵 블레셋 사람들이 이스라엘과 전쟁을 하려고 모든 군대를 모았다. 아기스가 다윗에게 말했다. "너도 알다시피, 너와 네 부하들은 나와 내 군대와 함께 싸우러 나가야 한다."

pt.L: E aconteceu naqueles dias que os filisteus reuniram os seus acampamentos para a guerra, para lutar contra Israel. E Aquis disse a Davi: "Saiba com certeza que você sairá comigo no acampamento, você e os seus homens."
pt.B: Naqueles dias os filisteus reuniram as suas forças para a guerra, para lutar contra Israel. Aquis disse a Davi: "Saiba bem disto: você e os seus homens vão sair comigo para a batalha, no meu exército."
pt.R: Naquele tempo os filisteus reuniram todas as suas tropas para ir à guerra contra Israel. Aquis disse a Davi: "Você sabe, é claro, que você e os seus homens vão marchar comigo e com o meu exército."

am.L: በዚያም ወራት ፍልስጥኤማውያን እስራኤልን ለመውጋት ሰፈሮቻቸውን ለጦርነት ሰበሰቡ። አንኩስም ዳዊትን፦ «አንተና ሰዎችህ ከእኔ ጋር ወደ ሰፈሩ እንደምትወጡ በእርግጥ ታውቃለህ» አለው።
am.B: በዚያ ዘመን ፍልስጥኤማውያን እስራኤልን ለመውጋት ሠራዊታቸውን ለጦርነት አሰባሰቡ። አንኩስም ዳዊትን፦ «ይህን በሚገባ እወቅ፤ አንተና ሰዎችህ ከእኔ ጋር በሠራዊቴ ውስጥ ሆናችሁ ወደ ጦርነት ትወጣላችሁ» አለው።
am.R: በዚያን ጊዜ ፍልስጥኤማውያን ከእስራኤል ጋር ለመዋጋት ወታደሮቻቸውን ሁሉ ሰበሰቡ። አንኩስም ዳዊትን፦ «አንተና ሰዎችህ ከእኔና ከሠራዊቴ ጋር እንደምትዘምቱ ታውቃለህ» አለው።

decisions.choice: their camps; the camp: the army, gathered in its camps
decisions.reason: The word means a camp, and from that the army that lives in it. The plural here pictures the troops of the several Philistine cities coming together (6:17-18; 29:2). In Achish's words, "the camp" is his own army.

decisions.choice: you surely know: Achish takes David's loyalty for granted
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: "knowing, you will know". Achish is not asking David; he is telling him what he expects of him. He believes David has made himself hated by Israel and will serve him for good (27:12).

decisions.choice: Achish and David: David is living as a vassal of the Philistine king of Gath
decisions.reason: David had fled from Saul to Achish king of Gath and been given the town of Ziklag (27:1-7). A vassal was expected to bring his men when his lord went to war, so David is caught between his host and his own people. The story of how he escapes the battle is told in 29:1-11.

decisions.choice: forces; army (Balanced); troops; army (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "forces", "troops" and "army" for the people in the camps, since "camps" alone would sound like the tents rather than the soldiers. Literal keeps "camps" and "camp".

decisions.choice: tú y tus hombres {{plural_you:saldrán|saldréis}}
decisions.reason: Achish speaks to David, but “you and your men” is a second person plural subject; Balanced and Readable put it first, so the verb is plural and takes the plural_you span. Literal follows the Hebrew order, with “saldrás” for David and “tú y tus hombres” added after.

decisions.choice: Achish speaks to David in the plain style (해라체); David answers in the formal polite style (합쇼체)
decisions.reason: As in chapter 27: David lives as a vassal of the Philistine king (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: você (Achish to David)
decisions.reason: Achish is the king and David his vassal (m3), so Achish says "você", as the king says to a subject throughout the book, while David answers him with "o senhor", "o rei" and "o seu servo" (27:5; verse 2).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in this chapter's Amharic
decisions.reason: The English of this chapter capitalises pronouns for God under the deity_pronoun setting (from verse 17). The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change in Amharic and the Amharic text carries no such spans.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־אָכִ֔ישׁ לָכֵן֙ אַתָּ֣ה תֵדַ֔ע אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אָכִישׁ֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד לָכֵ֗ן שֹׁמֵ֧ר לְרֹאשִׁ֛י אֲשִֽׂימְךָ֖ כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Achish, Therefore you will know what will do your servant. And said Achish to David, Therefore [a] keeper of my head I will make you all the days.

en.L: And David said to Achish, "Therefore you will know what your servant will do." And Achish said to David, "Therefore I will make you keeper of my head all the days."
en.B: David answered Achish, "Very well, you will see for yourself what your servant will do." Achish said to David, "Very well, I will make you my bodyguard for life."
en.R: David answered, "Good. Then you will see for yourself what I will do." Achish said, "Good. I will make you my own bodyguard for as long as you live."

es.L: Y dijo David a Aquis: «Por eso sabrás lo que hará tu siervo». Y dijo Aquis a David: «Por eso te haré guarda de mi cabeza todos los días».
es.B: David le respondió a Aquis: «Muy bien, verás por ti mismo lo que tu siervo es capaz de hacer». Aquis le dijo a David: «Muy bien, te haré mi guardaespaldas de por vida».
es.R: David le respondió: «Bien. Entonces verás por ti mismo lo que voy a hacer». Aquis le dijo: «Bien. Te haré mi guardaespaldas personal por el resto de tu vida».

fr.L: Et David dit à Akish : « Eh bien, tu sauras ce que fera ton serviteur. » Et Akish dit à David : « Eh bien, je ferai de toi le gardien de ma tête pour toujours. »
fr.B: David répondit à Akish : « Très bien, tu verras toi-même ce que ton serviteur est capable de faire. » Akish dit à David : « Très bien, je ferai de toi mon garde du corps pour toujours. »
fr.R: David a répondu : « Bien. Alors tu verras toi-même ce que je ferai. » Akish a dit : « Bien. Je ferai de toi mon propre garde du corps pour toute ta vie. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia Akishi, "Kwa hiyo utajua atakalofanya mtumishi wako." Akishi akamwambia Daudi, "Kwa hiyo nitakufanya mlinzi wa kichwa changu siku zote."
sw.B: Daudi akamjibu Akishi, "Vyema, utajionea mwenyewe atakalofanya mtumishi wako." Akishi akamwambia Daudi, "Vyema, nitakufanya mlinzi wangu maisha yako yote."
sw.R: Daudi akajibu, "Vyema. Basi utaona mwenyewe nitakalofanya mimi mtumishi wako." Akishi akasema, "Vyema. Nitakufanya mlinzi wangu binafsi maisha yako yote."

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với A-kích: "Vì vậy vua sẽ biết đầy tớ của vua sẽ làm gì." A-kích nói với Đa-vít: "Vì vậy ta sẽ lập ngươi làm người giữ đầu ta suốt mọi ngày."
vi.B: Đa-vít đáp với A-kích: "Được lắm, bệ hạ sẽ tự thấy đầy tớ của bệ hạ sẽ làm gì." A-kích nói với Đa-vít: "Được lắm, ta sẽ lập ngươi làm cận vệ của ta suốt đời."
vi.R: Đa-vít đáp: "Tốt lắm. Rồi đức vua sẽ tự thấy tôi sẽ làm gì." A-kích nói: "Tốt lắm. Ta sẽ cho ngươi làm cận vệ riêng của ta suốt đời."

ko.L: 그러자 다윗이 아기스에게 말했다. "그러면 임금님의 종이 무엇을 할지 임금님께서 아시게 될 것입니다." 그러자 아기스가 다윗에게 말했다. "그러면 내가 너를 평생 내 머리를 지키는 자로 삼겠다."
ko.B: 다윗이 아기스에게 대답했다. "좋습니다. 임금님의 종이 무엇을 할 수 있는지 직접 보시게 될 것입니다." 아기스가 다윗에게 말했다. "좋다. 내가 너를 평생 내 경호대장으로 삼겠다."
ko.R: 다윗이 대답했다. "좋습니다. 제가 무엇을 하는지 직접 보시게 될 것입니다." 아기스가 말했다. "좋다. 너를 평생 내 경호대장으로 삼겠다."

pt.L: E Davi disse a Aquis: "Pois bem, o senhor saberá o que o seu servo fará." E Aquis disse a Davi: "Pois bem, farei de você o guarda da minha cabeça por todos os dias."
pt.B: Davi respondeu a Aquis: "Muito bem, o rei verá por si mesmo o que o seu servo fará." Aquis disse a Davi: "Muito bem, farei de você o meu guarda-costas pela vida toda."
pt.R: Davi respondeu: "Ótimo. Então o senhor vai ver com os próprios olhos o que eu vou fazer." Aquis disse: "Ótimo. Vou fazer de você o meu guarda-costas pelo resto da sua vida."

am.L: ዳዊትም አንኩስን፦ «ስለዚህ ባሪያዎ የሚያደርገውን ያውቃሉ» አለው። አንኩስም ዳዊትን፦ «ስለዚህ በዘመኑ ሁሉ የራሴ ጠባቂ አደርግሃለሁ» አለው።
am.B: ዳዊትም አንኩስን፦ «መልካም፣ አገልጋይዎ የሚያደርገውን ራስዎ ያያሉ» ብሎ መለሰለት። አንኩስም ዳዊትን፦ «መልካም፣ በዕድሜ ልክህ የግል ጠባቂዬ አደርግሃለሁ» አለው።
am.R: ዳዊትም፦ «መልካም፣ እንግዲያው እኔ የማደርገውን ራስዎ ያያሉ» ብሎ መለሰ። አንኩስም፦ «መልካም፣ በሕይወትህ ዘመን ሁሉ የግል ጠባቂዬ አደርግሃለሁ» አለው።

decisions.choice: you will know what your servant will do: an answer that can be heard two ways
decisions.reason: Achish hears a promise to fight well for him. But David does not say whose side he will fight on, and the reader knows he has been deceiving Achish about his raids (27:8-12). The words are left open, as David leaves them; the question is settled only when the Philistine commanders send him away (29:4-11).

decisions.choice: therefore: very well, in that case
decisions.reason: The word usually means "therefore". Here each man uses it to take up what the other has said: "if that is so, then ...". Achish's reply rewards David in advance for what he expects David to do.

decisions.choice: keeper of my head: my bodyguard
decisions.reason: The one who guards the king's head is the guard closest to his person. Achish gives David the highest mark of trust. "All the days" means for the rest of David's life.

decisions.choice: your servant: a polite way of saying "I"
decisions.reason: Speaking of oneself as "your servant" was the humble form of address to a king or lord (17:32, 34; 20:7).

decisions.choice: I
decisions.reason: Readable puts the polite "your servant" into the plain "I". Literal and Balanced keep the humble form of address.

decisions.choice: lo que tu siervo es capaz de hacer (B)
decisions.reason: David's answer can be heard two ways (m1); Spanish keeps it open: Achish hears a promise, the reader may hear a warning.

decisions.choice: "임금님의 종이 무엇을 할지" kept open, as the Hebrew
decisions.reason: David's answer can be heard two ways (meaning decision m1); Korean keeps it as ambiguous as the Hebrew and does not say for whom David will act.

decisions.choice: o que o seu servo fará (L, B); o que eu vou fazer (R)
alternatives: o que o seu servo é capaz de fazer
decisions.reason: David's answer is left open, as m1 says the Hebrew leaves it: Portuguese says only what he "will do", not for whom or against whom. Balanced has David call Achish "o rei", the courtly third person, beside "o seu servo".

decisions.choice: "የራሴ ጠባቂ" (keeper of my head) at Literal; "የግል ጠባቂዬ" (my bodyguard) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Amharic "ራስ" means both "head" and "self", so the literal phrase is understood as "my own guard" (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable use the ordinary word.

source.text: וּשְׁמוּאֵ֣ל מֵ֔ת וַיִּסְפְּדוּ־לוֹ֙ כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֥הוּ בָרָמָ֖ה וּבְעִיר֑וֹ וְשָׁא֗וּל הֵסִ֛יר הָאֹב֥וֹת וְאֶת־הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֖ים מֵהָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Samuel had died, and mourned for him all Israel, and they buried him in Ramah, even in his city; and Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.

en.L: Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, in his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.
en.B: Now Samuel was dead. All Israel had mourned for him, and they had buried him in Ramah, his own town. And Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.
en.R: Samuel had died some time before. All the people of Israel had mourned for him, and they had buried him in Ramah, his hometown. Saul had also forced out of the land the people who say they can talk with the dead or with spirits.

es.L: Y Samuel había muerto, y todo Israel había hecho duelo por él, y lo habían sepultado en Ramá, en su propia ciudad. Y Saúl había expulsado de la tierra a los médiums y a los espiritistas.
es.B: Samuel ya había muerto. Todo Israel había hecho duelo por él, y lo habían sepultado en Ramá, su ciudad. Y Saúl había expulsado de la tierra a los médiums y a los espiritistas.
es.R: Samuel había muerto algún tiempo antes. Todo el pueblo de Israel había hecho duelo por él, y lo habían sepultado en Ramá, su pueblo. Saúl también había echado del país a la gente que dice que puede hablar con los muertos o con los espíritus.

fr.L: Or Samuel était mort, et tout Israël avait mené le deuil sur lui, et on l’avait enterré à Rama, dans sa ville. Et Saül avait ôté du pays les nécromanciens et les devins.
fr.B: Samuel était mort. Tout Israël l’avait pleuré, et on l’avait enterré à Rama, sa ville. Et Saül avait chassé du pays les nécromanciens et les devins.
fr.R: Samuel était mort quelque temps avant. Tout le peuple d’Israël l’avait pleuré, et on l’avait enterré à Rama, sa ville. Saül avait aussi chassé du pays les gens qui prétendent parler avec les morts ou avec les esprits.

sw.L: Basi Samweli alikuwa amekufa, na Israeli wote walikuwa wamemwombolezea na kumzika Rama, katika mji wake mwenyewe. Naye Sauli alikuwa amewaondoa katika nchi wanaowaita wafu na wapiga ramli.
sw.B: Samweli alikuwa amekwisha kufa. Israeli wote walikuwa wamemwombolezea, nao walikuwa wamemzika Rama, mji wake mwenyewe. Naye Sauli alikuwa amewaondoa katika nchi wanaowaita wafu na wapiga ramli.
sw.R: Samweli alikuwa amekufa muda fulani kabla. Watu wote wa Israeli walikuwa wamemwombolezea, nao walikuwa wamemzika Rama, mji wake. Sauli alikuwa pia amewafukuza katika nchi watu wanaodai kwamba wanaweza kuongea na wafu au na pepo.

vi.L: Bấy giờ Sa-mu-ên đã qua đời; cả Y-sơ-ra-ên đã khóc thương ông và chôn ông tại Ra-ma, tức là thành của ông. Còn Sau-lơ đã trừ bỏ các đồng cốt và thầy chiêu hồn khỏi xứ.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Sa-mu-ên đã qua đời. Toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã khóc thương ông, và họ đã chôn ông tại Ra-ma, quê nhà của ông. Còn Sau-lơ đã trừ bỏ các đồng cốt và thầy chiêu hồn khỏi xứ.
vi.R: Sa-mu-ên đã qua đời trước đó ít lâu. Toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã khóc thương ông, và họ đã chôn ông tại Ra-ma, quê nhà của ông. Sau-lơ cũng đã đuổi ra khỏi xứ những người nói rằng mình có thể nói chuyện với người chết hay với các vong linh.

ko.L: 그때 사무엘은 이미 죽었고, 온 이스라엘이 그를 위해 슬퍼하며 그를 그의 성읍 라마에 묻었다. 그리고 사울은 영매들과 무당들을 그 땅에서 쫓아냈었다.
ko.B: 사무엘은 이미 죽었다. 온 이스라엘이 그를 애도하고 그의 고향 라마에 장사 지냈다. 그리고 사울은 영매들과 무당들을 그 땅에서 쫓아냈었다.
ko.R: 사무엘은 얼마 전에 죽었다. 이스라엘의 모든 백성이 그의 죽음을 슬퍼했고, 그를 그의 고향 라마에 묻었다. 그리고 사울은 죽은 사람이나 영들과 이야기할 수 있다고 하는 사람들을 그 땅에서 쫓아냈었다.

pt.L: E Samuel tinha morrido, e todo o Israel o tinha pranteado e o tinha sepultado em Ramá, na sua própria cidade. E Saul tinha removido da terra os médiuns e os espíritas.
pt.B: Ora, Samuel estava morto. Todo o Israel o tinha pranteado, e o tinham sepultado em Ramá, a sua cidade. E Saul tinha banido da terra os médiuns e os espíritas.
pt.R: Samuel tinha morrido algum tempo antes. Todo o povo de Israel tinha chorado a morte dele, e ele tinha sido sepultado em Ramá, a cidade onde morava. Saul também tinha expulsado do país as pessoas que dizem que podem falar com os mortos ou com os espíritos.

am.L: ሳሙኤልም ሞቶ ነበር፤ እስራኤልም ሁሉ አልቅሰውለት በከተማው በራማ ቀብረውት ነበር። ሳኦልም ሙታን ጠሪዎችንና ጠንቋዮችን ከምድሪቱ አስወግዶ ነበር።
am.B: ሳሙኤል ሞቶ ነበር። እስራኤል ሁሉ አልቅሰውለት በገዛ ከተማው በራማ ቀብረውት ነበር። ሳኦልም ሙታን ጠሪዎችንና ጠንቋዮችን ከምድሪቱ አስወግዶ ነበር።
am.R: ሳሙኤል ከዚያ ጥቂት ጊዜ በፊት ሞቶ ነበር። የእስራኤል ሕዝብ ሁሉ አልቅሰውለት በትውልድ ከተማው በራማ ቀብረውት ነበር። ሳኦልም ከሙታን ወይም ከመናፍስት ጋር እንነጋገራለን የሚሉትን ሰዎች ከምድሪቱ አባርሮ ነበር።

decisions.choice: Samuel had died ... Saul had removed: background, told before the story begins
decisions.reason: Both clauses put the subject first and use a verb form that looks back. They are not new events but two facts the reader needs for what follows: Samuel, whom Saul will ask for, is dead, and the people Saul will go to have been banned by Saul himself.

decisions.choice: Samuel's death and burial repeat 25:1
decisions.reason: Samuel's death, Israel's mourning and his burial at Ramah were told in 25:1 in almost the same words. They are repeated here to set the scene.

decisions.choice: the mediums and the spiritists: people who claimed to call up the dead and learn from them
decisions.reason: These are the two words forbidden together in Leviticus 19:31; 20:6, 27 and Deuteronomy 18:11. The first may name the spirit of a dead person, or the pit through which it was called up, or the one who called it; in this chapter it is used both for the people (verses 3, 9) and for the spirit (verses 7, 8). The second comes from the verb "know" and names one who claims secret knowledge from the spirits.

decisions.choice: Saul had removed them: he had kept the law against them
decisions.reason: The law forbade consulting such people and made them liable to death (Leviticus 20:27; Deuteronomy 18:10-12). Saul had once enforced it; the woman says in verse 9 that he "cut them off". The story turns on his doing what he himself had banned.

decisions.choice: the people who say they can talk with the dead or with spirits
decisions.reason: Readable describes what mediums and spiritists claimed to do, as at Leviticus 19:31. It adds "some time before" to show that Samuel's death is not part of the new events.

decisions.choice: les nécromanciens et les devins
decisions.reason: The two words for those who claimed to call up the dead (m3); "nécromancien" says the first plainly, "devin" the second; "médium" and "spirite" sound modern in French. Readable describes them, as the English (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: los médiums y los espiritistas (L, B); la gente que dice que puede hablar con los muertos o con los espíritus (R)
decisions.reason: People who claimed to call up the dead (m3). Spanish has plain words for both, as the English has; Readable explains them, as the English does (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: "wanaowaita wafu na wapiga ramli" (L, B); described at R
decisions.reason: As the Swahili of Leviticus 19:31 and 20:6: Swahili has no single word for a medium, so the first is described by what the medium does, and "mpiga ramli" names the one who seeks hidden knowledge. Readable describes both, as Leviticus does.

decisions.choice: "các đồng cốt và thầy chiêu hồn" (L, B); explained at R
decisions.reason: People who claimed to call up the dead and learn from them (m3); "thầy bói" is a fortune-teller, which is not what the words mean.

decisions.choice: "영매들과 무당들" (mediums and spiritists) at Literal and Balanced; Readable describes them
decisions.reason: People who claimed to call up the dead (meaning decision m3); "영매" and "무당" are current Korean words, "신접한 자" and "박수" the older ones.

decisions.choice: os médiuns e os espíritas (L, B); as pessoas que dizem que podem falar com os mortos ou com os espíritos (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also verse 9): the pair forbidden in Leviticus 19:31 and Deuteronomy 18:11 (m3), in the words those passages use in Portuguese, level by level, so the link with the law can be heard. As Leviticus 19:31 notes, "espírita" in Brazil also names followers of Spiritism, a present-day religion; the verse speaks of the ancient practice. Readable describes the claim, as Leviticus 19:31 does.

decisions.choice: "ሙታን ጠሪዎች" for the mediums and "ጠንቋዮች" for the spiritists (L, B); Readable describes them
decisions.reason: The words of Leviticus 19:31 and 20:6, 27, which name the same two practices; Readable uses the description Leviticus uses at that level. The same in verse 9.

source.text: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְשׁוּנֵ֑ם וַיִּקְבֹּ֤ץ שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּגִּלְבֹּֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered [the] Philistines and came and encamped at Shunem; and gathered Saul all Israel, and they encamped at Gilboa.

en.L: And the Philistines gathered and came and camped at Shunem; and Saul gathered all Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.
en.B: The Philistines assembled and came and camped at Shunem, and Saul gathered all Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.
en.R: The Philistines came together and set up camp at the town of Shunem. Saul called together all the fighting men of Israel, and they set up camp on Mount Gilboa.

es.L: Y se reunieron los filisteos, y vinieron y acamparon en Sunem; y reunió Saúl a todo Israel, y acamparon en Gilboa.
es.B: Los filisteos se reunieron y vinieron a acampar en Sunem, y Saúl reunió a todo Israel, y acamparon en Gilboa.
es.R: Los filisteos se juntaron y pusieron su campamento en el pueblo de Sunem. Saúl reunió a todos los hombres de guerra de Israel, y pusieron su campamento en el monte Gilboa.

fr.L: Et les Philistins se rassemblèrent, et ils vinrent camper à Shounem ; et Saül rassembla tout Israël, et ils campèrent à Guilboa.
fr.B: Les Philistins se rassemblèrent et vinrent camper à Shounem, et Saül rassembla tout Israël, et ils campèrent à Guilboa.
fr.R: Les Philistins se sont rassemblés et ils ont installé leur camp à Shounem. Saül a rassemblé tous les soldats d’Israël, et ils ont installé leur camp sur le mont Guilboa.

sw.L: Wafilisti wakakusanyika, wakaja, wakapiga kambi Shunemu; naye Sauli akawakusanya Israeli wote, wakapiga kambi Gilboa.
sw.B: Wafilisti wakakusanyika, wakaja, wakapiga kambi Shunemu, naye Sauli akawakusanya Israeli wote, wakapiga kambi Gilboa.
sw.R: Wafilisti wakakusanyika, wakapiga kambi katika mji wa Shunemu. Sauli akawakusanya wapiganaji wote wa Israeli, nao wakapiga kambi katika mlima Gilboa.

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin tập hợp lại, đến đóng trại tại Su-nem; Sau-lơ tập hợp cả Y-sơ-ra-ên, và họ đóng trại tại Ghinh-bô-a.
vi.B: Người Phi-li-tin tập hợp lại, kéo đến đóng trại tại Su-nem, còn Sau-lơ tập hợp toàn quân Y-sơ-ra-ên và đóng trại tại Ghinh-bô-a.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin tụ họp lại và đóng trại tại thành Su-nem. Sau-lơ triệu tập tất cả những người lính của Y-sơ-ra-ên, và họ đóng trại trên núi Ghinh-bô-a.

ko.L: 그리고 블레셋 사람들이 모여 와서 수넴에 진을 쳤고, 사울은 온 이스라엘을 모아 길보아에 진을 쳤다.
ko.B: 블레셋 사람들이 모여 와서 수넴에 진을 쳤고, 사울도 온 이스라엘을 모아 길보아에 진을 쳤다.
ko.R: 블레셋 사람들이 모여 와서 수넴 마을에 진을 쳤다. 사울은 이스라엘의 모든 군인을 불러 모았고, 그들은 길보아 산에 진을 쳤다.

pt.L: E os filisteus se reuniram, e vieram e acamparam em Suném; e Saul reuniu todo o Israel, e acamparam em Gilboa.
pt.B: Os filisteus se reuniram, vieram e acamparam em Suném, e Saul reuniu todo o Israel, e eles acamparam em Gilboa.
pt.R: Os filisteus se juntaram e armaram o acampamento na cidade de Suném. Saul reuniu todos os homens de guerra de Israel, e eles armaram o acampamento no monte Gilboa.

am.L: ፍልስጥኤማውያንም ተሰብስበው መጡ፤ በሱነምም ሰፈሩ፤ ሳኦልም እስራኤልን ሁሉ ሰበሰበ፤ በጊልቦዓም ሰፈሩ።
am.B: ፍልስጥኤማውያን ተሰብስበው መጡ፤ በሱነምም ሰፈሩ። ሳኦልም እስራኤልን ሁሉ ሰበሰበ፤ እነርሱም በጊልቦዓ ሰፈሩ።
am.R: ፍልስጥኤማውያን ተሰብስበው በሱነም ከተማ ሰፈሩ። ሳኦልም የእስራኤልን ተዋጊዎች ሁሉ ሰበሰበ፤ እነርሱም በጊልቦዓ ተራራ ሰፈሩ።

decisions.choice: Shunem and Gilboa: two heights facing each other across the valley of Jezreel
decisions.reason: Shunem was a town in Issachar (Joshua 19:18) on the slope of the hill of Moreh, on the north side of the valley. Gilboa is the ridge on the south side. The Philistines had marched far north of their own land, into the broad valley where their chariots could move (31:1-3; 2 Samuel 1:6).

decisions.choice: all Israel: the whole army of Israel
decisions.reason: Saul gathers the fighting men from the tribes, not every person in Israel.

decisions.choice: the order of the story
decisions.reason: Chapter 29 begins with the Philistines gathering at Aphek, before they went up to Jezreel (29:1, 11). The writer tells Saul's night at Endor first and then goes back to tell what happened to David at the same time. The battle itself is told in chapter 31.

decisions.choice: the town of Shunem; Mount Gilboa; the fighting men of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of place each name is, and that "all Israel" here means Israel's soldiers.

decisions.choice: Shounem; Guilboa
decisions.reason: Shounem, a name not in the terms table, in the usual French transcription; Guilboa as the Samuel terms note sets, with "le mont" at Readable.

decisions.choice: "Shunemu"; "Gilboa", "mlima Gilboa" (R)
decisions.reason: "Mlima Gilboa" as the terms note; "Shunemu" takes a Swahili spelling and is kept through the block.

decisions.choice: "Su-nem"; "Ghinh-bô-a" (R: "núi Ghinh-bô-a")
decisions.reason: "Ghinh-bô-a" as the terms note; "Su-nem" in the usual Protestant form.

decisions.choice: "수넴", "길보아" (R: "길보아 산")
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant Korean forms; "길보아 산" is the form the terms of this translation set.

decisions.choice: Suném; Gilboa (L, B), o monte Gilboa (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 29:1; 31:1, 8): "Suném", the form of Joshua 19:18 in Portuguese, with the accent its stress needs; "Gilboa" as the name, and "o monte Gilboa", with "monte" in lowercase as an ordinary noun, where the text or the Readable names the ridge (31:1). "Gelboé" is the older form from the Latin.

decisions.choice: "ሱነም" for Shunem and "ጊልቦዓ" for Gilboa
decisions.reason: The names in their usual Ethiopian Bible forms, kept through chapters 28-31.

records.literal_gloss: And saw Saul the camp of [the] Philistines, and he was afraid, and trembled his heart greatly.

en.L: And Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, and he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.
en.B: When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid, and his heart shook violently.
en.R: When Saul saw the Philistine army, he became afraid. He was shaking with fear inside.

es.L: Y vio Saúl el campamento de los filisteos, y tuvo miedo, y su corazón tembló en gran manera.
es.B: Cuando Saúl vio el ejército filisteo, tuvo miedo, y el corazón le temblaba con violencia.
es.R: Cuando Saúl vio el ejército filisteo, tuvo miedo. Temblaba de miedo por dentro.

fr.L: Et Saül vit le camp des Philistins, et il eut peur, et son cœur trembla beaucoup.
fr.B: Quand Saül vit l’armée des Philistins, il eut peur, et son cœur se mit à trembler violemment.
fr.R: Quand Saül a vu l’armée des Philistins, il a eu peur. Il tremblait de peur au fond de lui.

sw.L: Sauli akaiona kambi ya Wafilisti, akaogopa, na moyo wake ukatetemeka sana.
sw.B: Sauli alipoliona jeshi la Wafilisti, akaogopa, na moyo wake ukatetemeka mno.
sw.R: Sauli alipoliona jeshi la Wafilisti, akaogopa. Akatetemeka kwa hofu moyoni mwake.

vi.L: Sau-lơ thấy trại quân Phi-li-tin thì sợ hãi, và lòng ông run rẩy dữ dội.
vi.B: Khi Sau-lơ thấy đạo quân Phi-li-tin, ông sợ hãi, lòng run lên bần bật.
vi.R: Khi Sau-lơ thấy đạo quân Phi-li-tin, ông trở nên sợ hãi. Trong lòng ông run rẩy vì sợ.

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 블레셋 사람들의 진영을 보고 두려워했고, 그의 마음이 크게 떨렸다.
ko.B: 사울은 블레셋 군대를 보고 두려워서 마음이 몹시 떨렸다.
ko.R: 사울은 블레셋 군대를 보고 겁이 났다. 그는 속으로 두려워 떨었다.

pt.L: E Saul viu o acampamento dos filisteus, e teve medo, e o seu coração tremeu muito.
pt.B: Quando Saul viu o exército filisteu, teve medo, e o seu coração estremeceu violentamente.
pt.R: Quando Saul viu o exército dos filisteus, ficou com medo. Por dentro, ele tremia de pavor.

am.L: ሳኦልም የፍልስጥኤማውያንን ሰፈር አየ፤ ፈራም፤ ልቡም እጅግ ተንቀጠቀጠ።
am.B: ሳኦል የፍልስጥኤማውያንን ሠራዊት ባየ ጊዜ ፈራ፤ ልቡም በኃይል ተናወጠ።
am.R: ሳኦል የፍልስጥኤማውያንን ሠራዊት ባየ ጊዜ ፈራ። ውስጡም በፍርሃት ይንቀጠቀጥ ነበር።

decisions.choice: his heart trembled greatly: he was filled with terror
decisions.reason: The heart is the inner person. Its trembling is deep fear, as when Eli's heart trembled for the ark (4:13). Saul and the army had been afraid before Goliath too (17:11), but then God had given David the victory.

decisions.choice: the camp of the Philistines: the Philistine army in its camp
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, the camp means the army encamped. From Gilboa Saul could look across the valley to Shunem.

decisions.choice: his heart shook violently (Balanced); he was shaking with fear inside (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the heart; Readable says plainly that the trembling was inward fear.

records.literal_gloss: And inquired Saul of Yahweh, and not answered him Yahweh, neither by dreams nor by Urim nor by prophets.

en.L: And Saul inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not answer him, neither by dreams nor by Urim nor by prophets.
en.B: Saul inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not answer him, whether by dreams or by the Urim or by prophets.
en.R: Saul asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} what he should do. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not answer him. He gave Saul no answer in dreams, or through the Urim the priest used, or through prophets.

es.L: Y consultó Saúl {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no le respondió, ni por sueños, ni por el urim, ni por profetas.
es.B: Saúl consultó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no le respondió, ni por sueños, ni por el urim, ni por medio de profetas.
es.R: Saúl le preguntó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} qué debía hacer. Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no le respondió. No le dio respuesta en sueños, ni por medio del urim que usaba el sacerdote, ni por medio de profetas.

fr.L: Et Saül consulta {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne lui répondit pas, ni par les songes, ni par les ourim, ni par les prophètes.
fr.B: Saül consulta {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne lui répondit pas, ni par des songes, ni par les ourim, ni par des prophètes.
fr.R: Saül a demandé {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ce qu’il devait faire. Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne lui a pas répondu. Il ne lui a donné aucune réponse, ni par des rêves, ni par les ourim dont le prêtre se servait, ni par des prophètes.

sw.L: Sauli akamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakumjibu, wala kwa ndoto, wala kwa Urimu, wala kwa manabii.
sw.B: Sauli akamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakumjibu, iwe kwa ndoto, au kwa Urimu, au kwa manabii.
sw.R: Sauli akamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} afanye nini. Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakumjibu. Hakumpa Sauli jibu kwa ndoto, wala kwa Urimu aliotumia kuhani, wala kupitia manabii.

vi.L: Sau-lơ cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không trả lời ông, hoặc bằng chiêm bao, hoặc bằng U-rim, hoặc bằng các nhà tiên tri.
vi.B: Sau-lơ cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không trả lời ông, dù qua chiêm bao, qua U-rim hay qua các nhà tiên tri.
vi.R: Sau-lơ cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xem mình phải làm gì. Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không trả lời ông. Ngài không trả lời Sau-lơ qua chiêm bao, cũng không qua U-rim mà thầy tế lễ dùng, cũng không qua các nhà tiên tri.

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈었으나, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 꿈으로도, 우림으로도, 예언자들로도 그에게 대답하지 않으셨다.
ko.B: 사울은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈었으나, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 꿈으로도, 우림으로도, 예언자들을 통해서도 그에게 대답하지 않으셨다.
ko.R: 사울은 어떻게 해야 할지 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈었다. 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 대답하지 않으셨다. 꿈으로도, 제사장이 쓰는 우림으로도, 예언자들을 통해서도 아무 대답을 주지 않으셨다.

pt.L: E Saul consultou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} não lhe respondeu, nem por sonhos, nem pelo Urim, nem por profetas.
pt.B: Saul consultou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} não lhe respondeu, nem por sonhos, nem pelo Urim, nem por meio de profetas.
pt.R: Saul perguntou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} o que devia fazer. Mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} não respondeu. Não deu nenhuma resposta a Saul, nem em sonhos, nem pelo Urim que o sacerdote usava, nem por meio de profetas.

am.L: ሳኦልም {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ጠየቀ፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ግን በሕልምም ቢሆን፣ በኡሪምም ቢሆን፣ በነቢያትም ቢሆን አልመለሰለትም።
am.B: ሳኦል {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ጠየቀ፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ግን በሕልም፣ በኡሪም ወይም በነቢያት አልመለሰለትም።
am.R: ሳኦል ምን ማድረግ እንዳለበት {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ጠየቀ። {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ግን አልመለሰለትም። በሕልምም ሆነ ካህኑ በሚጠቀምበት በኡሪም ወይም በነቢያት በኩል ምንም መልስ አልሰጠውም።

decisions.choice: the LORD did not answer him: the silence of God toward Saul
decisions.reason: Dreams, the priest's lots and prophets were the ways God was known to answer his people (Numbers 12:6; 27:21; Deuteronomy 18:15). None of them answers Saul. God had already been silent once when Saul asked (14:37), and the Spirit of Yahweh had left him (16:14). 1 Chronicles 10:13-14 gives the outcome: Saul died because he consulted a medium and did not seek Yahweh.

decisions.choice: Urim: the sacred lots by which the priest asked God for a decision
decisions.reason: The Urim were kept by the high priest with the ephod (Exodus 28:30; Numbers 27:21; 14:41 in this book). The priest Abiathar had fled to David with the ephod after Saul killed the priests of Nob (22:20; 23:6, 9). The text does not say how Saul inquired by Urim; another priest may have served him.

decisions.choice: inquired: asked God for guidance
decisions.reason: The verb "ask" sounds like Saul's own name, which means "asked for". The man whom the people asked for as king (8:10; 12:13) now asks and is not answered.

decisions.choice: the Urim the priest used; He gave Saul no answer
decisions.reason: Readable adds who used the Urim, and repeats the verb so that each of the three ways stands clearly.

decisions.choice: les ourim
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for the Urim; Readable adds who used them, as the English (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: el urim
decisions.reason: The sacred lots by which the priest asked God for a decision (m2), named as the Samuel terms note sets; Readable explains it, as the English does (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: "우림" for the Urim
decisions.reason: The form the terms of this translation set; Readable adds that the priest used it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: consultou ao SENHOR; o Urim
decisions.reason: "Consultar a Deus" is the form of 14:37 in Portuguese for asking God for guidance (m3), so the name takes the same preposition here. The Urim keep the name of Exodus 28:30 and of 14:41 (m2), "o Urim", alone as the Hebrew has it; Readable says who used them, as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: And said Saul to his servants, Seek for me a woman, a mistress of a spirit, and I will go to her and inquire of her. And said his servants to him, Behold, a woman, a mistress of a spirit, at Endor.

en.L: And Saul said to his servants, "Seek out for me a woman who is mistress of a spirit, so that I may go to her and inquire of her." And his servants said to him, "Look, [there is] a woman who is mistress of a spirit at Endor."
en.B: Saul told his servants, "Look for a woman who is a medium, so that I may go and inquire through her." His servants answered him, "There is a woman at Endor who is a medium."
en.R: Saul told his servants, "Find a woman for me who can call up the spirits of the dead. I will go to her and ask her what to do." His servants answered, "There is a woman like that at Endor."

es.L: Y dijo Saúl a sus siervos: «{{plural_you:Búsquenme|Buscadme}} una mujer que sea dueña de un espíritu, para que yo vaya a ella y le consulte». Y le dijeron sus siervos: «He aquí [que hay] una mujer dueña de un espíritu en Endor».
es.B: Saúl les dijo a sus siervos: «{{plural_you:Búsquenme|Buscadme}} una mujer que sea médium, para que yo vaya y consulte por medio de ella». Sus siervos le respondieron: «En Endor hay una mujer que es médium».
es.R: Saúl les dijo a sus siervos: «{{plural_you:Encuéntrenme|Encontradme}} una mujer que pueda llamar a los espíritus de los muertos. Iré a verla y le preguntaré qué hacer». Sus siervos le contestaron: «En Endor hay una mujer así».

fr.L: Et Saül dit à ses serviteurs : « Cherchez-moi une femme qui soit maîtresse d’un esprit, et j’irai vers elle et je la consulterai. » Et ses serviteurs lui dirent : « Voici, [il y a] une femme maîtresse d’un esprit à Endor. »
fr.B: Saül dit à ses serviteurs : « Cherchez-moi une femme qui évoque les morts, pour que j’aille la consulter. » Ses serviteurs lui répondirent : « Il y a à Endor une femme qui évoque les morts. »
fr.R: Saül a dit à ses serviteurs : « Trouvez-moi une femme qui sait faire venir les esprits des morts. J’irai la voir et je lui demanderai ce que je dois faire. » Ses serviteurs lui ont répondu : « Il y a une femme comme ça à Endor. »

sw.L: Sauli akawaambia watumishi wake, "Nitafutieni mwanamke aliye bibi wa mzimu, ili niende kwake nikamwulize." Watumishi wake wakamwambia, "Tazama, [yuko] mwanamke aliye bibi wa mzimu huko Endori."
sw.B: Sauli akawaambia watumishi wake, "Nitafutieni mwanamke anayewaita wafu, ili niende nikaulize kupitia kwake." Watumishi wake wakamjibu, "Yuko mwanamke huko Endori anayewaita wafu."
sw.R: Sauli akawaambia watumishi wake, "Nitafutieni mwanamke anayeweza kuziita roho za wafu. Nitakwenda kwake nimwulize nifanye nini." Watumishi wake wakajibu, "Yuko mwanamke wa namna hiyo huko Endori."

vi.L: Sau-lơ nói với các đầy tớ mình: "Hãy tìm cho ta một người đàn bà làm chủ một vong linh, để ta đến với bà ấy và cầu hỏi bà ấy." Các đầy tớ thưa với ông: "Kìa, có một người đàn bà làm chủ một vong linh tại Ên-đô-rơ."
vi.B: Sau-lơ bảo các đầy tớ: "Hãy tìm cho ta một bà đồng cốt, để ta đến đó cầu hỏi qua bà ấy." Các đầy tớ thưa với ông: "Ở Ên-đô-rơ có một bà đồng cốt."
vi.R: Sau-lơ bảo các đầy tớ: "Hãy tìm cho ta một người đàn bà có thể gọi hồn người chết. Ta sẽ đến hỏi bà ấy xem ta phải làm gì." Các đầy tớ thưa: "Ở Ên-đô-rơ có một người đàn bà như thế."

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 그의 신하들에게 말했다. "영을 부리는 여자를 나를 위해 찾아라. 내가 그 여자에게 가서 물어보겠다." 그러자 그의 신하들이 그에게 말했다. "보십시오, 엔돌에 영을 부리는 여자가 있습니다."
ko.B: 사울이 신하들에게 말했다. "영매 노릇을 하는 여자를 찾아라. 내가 그 여자에게 가서 물어보겠다." 신하들이 그에게 대답했다. "엔돌에 영매 노릇을 하는 여자가 있습니다."
ko.R: 사울이 신하들에게 말했다. "죽은 사람의 영을 불러올 수 있는 여자를 찾아 다오. 내가 그 여자에게 가서 어떻게 해야 할지 물어보겠다." 신하들이 대답했다. "엔돌에 그런 여자가 있습니다."

pt.L: E Saul disse aos seus servos: "Procurem para mim uma mulher que [seja] senhora de um espírito, e irei até ela e a consultarei." E os seus servos lhe disseram: "Eis [que há] uma mulher que [é] senhora de um espírito em En-Dor."
pt.B: Saul ordenou aos seus servos: "Procurem uma mulher que seja médium, para que eu vá até ela e faça a consulta por meio dela." Os seus servos lhe responderam: "Há em En-Dor uma mulher que é médium."
pt.R: Saul disse aos seus servos: "Encontrem para mim uma mulher que saiba chamar os espíritos dos mortos. Eu vou até ela perguntar o que devo fazer." Os servos responderam: "Há uma mulher assim em En-Dor."

am.L: ሳኦልም ባሪያዎቹን፦ «ወደ እርሷ ሄጄ እንድጠይቃት የመንፈስ እመቤት የሆነች ሴት ፈልጉልኝ» አላቸው። ባሪያዎቹም፦ «እነሆ፣ በዓይንዶር የመንፈስ እመቤት የሆነች ሴት [አለች]» አሉት።
am.B: ሳኦል ሹማምንቱን፦ «ሄጄ በእርሷ በኩል እንድጠይቅ ሙታን ጠሪ የሆነች ሴት ፈልጉልኝ» አላቸው። ሹማምንቱም፦ «በዓይንዶር ሙታን ጠሪ የሆነች አንዲት ሴት አለች» ብለው መለሱለት።
am.R: ሳኦል ሹማምንቱን፦ «የሙታንን መናፍስት መጥራት የምትችል ሴት ፈልጉልኝ። ወደ እርሷ ሄጄ ምን ማድረግ እንዳለብኝ እጠይቃታለሁ» አላቸው። ሹማምንቱም፦ «በዓይንዶር እንደዚህ ያለች ሴት አለች» ብለው መለሱለት።

decisions.choice: a woman who is mistress of a spirit: a woman who claims to call up and control a spirit of the dead
alternatives: a woman who owns a spirit pit
decisions.reason: Literally "a woman, a mistress of an 'ov". Here 'ov names the spirit, or the means of calling it, and the woman is its "owner" or "mistress", the one who has power over it. She is one of the mediums Saul himself had banned (verse 3).

decisions.choice: inquire of her: seek from the dead what only God can tell
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual one for seeking God's word (9:9). The law forbids seeking it from the dead (Deuteronomy 18:11), and Isaiah 8:19 asks why a people should seek the dead on behalf of the living instead of their God.

decisions.choice: Endor: a town on the north side of the hill of Moreh
decisions.reason: Endor lay in the land of Manasseh (Joshua 17:11), a few miles north of Shunem. To reach it from Gilboa, Saul had to go around the Philistine camp, which is one reason he went by night and in disguise (verse 8).

decisions.choice: his servants: Saul's attendants
decisions.reason: These are the men who served the king closely, here trusted to find the woman and keep the visit secret (verses 8, 23, 25).

decisions.choice: a woman who is a medium (Balanced); a woman who can call up the spirits of the dead (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the word "medium" used for this practice in Leviticus 19:31 and Deuteronomy 18:11; Readable says what she claimed to do. Literal keeps the Hebrew picture, "mistress of a spirit".

decisions.choice: une femme maîtresse d'un esprit (L); une femme qui évoque les morts (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase (m1); Balanced says what she claimed to do, and avoids "sorcière", which brings in later ideas the text does not have.

decisions.choice: una mujer dueña de un espíritu (L); una médium (B); una mujer que pueda llamar a los espíritus de los muertos (R)
decisions.reason: A woman who claims to call up and control a spirit of the dead (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew “mistress of a spirit”; Balanced uses the word of verse 3; Readable explains, as the English does (r-en-1). “Siervos” at Literal and Balanced here, as the English keeps “servants” for Saul's attendants.

decisions.choice: "aliye bibi wa mzimu" (L); "anayewaita wafu" (B); "anayeweza kuziita roho za wafu" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mistress of" and uses "mzimu", the spirit of a dead person (m1); Balanced uses the description chosen for mediums in Leviticus, and Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "người đàn bà làm chủ một vong linh" (L); "bà đồng cốt" (B); "người đàn bà có thể gọi hồn người chết" (R)
decisions.reason: A woman who claims to call up and control a spirit of the dead (m1); Literal keeps the Hebrew's "mistress of a spirit".

decisions.choice: "영을 부리는 여자" (L), "영매 노릇을 하는 여자" (B), "죽은 사람의 영을 불러올 수 있는 여자" (R); "엔돌"
decisions.reason: A woman who claims to call up and control a spirit of the dead (meaning decision m1); "엔돌" is the form the terms of this translation set.

decisions.choice: senhora de um espírito (L); médium (B); que saiba chamar os espíritos dos mortos (R); En-Dor
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the woman is "a médium de En-Dor", with the word Balanced uses for the "mediums" of verse 3, as the English does; "feiticeira", the old name, says witchcraft, which the text does not. Literal keeps the Hebrew picture with "senhora", the one who has power over the spirit (m1). "En-Dor" is written in two parts joined by a hyphen, as Brazilian Bibles write the name and as "Bete-Semes".

decisions.choice: "የመንፈስ እመቤት" (mistress of a spirit) at Literal; "ሙታን ጠሪ" (medium) at Balanced, as Leviticus 19:31
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase, a woman who has a spirit at her command (meaning decision m1); Balanced uses the name of the practice that Leviticus gives, and Readable describes it.

decisions.choice: Saul's servants are "ባሪያዎቹ" (L) and "ሹማምንቱ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: A king's servants follow the Pentateuch ruling for Pharaoh's (meaning decision m4: Saul's attendants); the same in verses 23 and 25.

source.text: וַיִּתְחַפֵּ֣שׂ שָׁא֗וּל וַיִּלְבַּשׁ֙ בְּגָדִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ ה֗וּא וּשְׁנֵ֤י אֲנָשִׁים֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל־הָאִשָּׁ֖ה לָ֑יְלָה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר קָֽסֳמִי־נָ֥אלִי֙ בָּא֔וֹב וְהַ֣עֲלִי לִ֔י אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־אֹמַ֖ר אֵלָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And disguised himself Saul and put on garments other, and went he and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night; and he said, Divine please for me by the spirit, and bring up for me whom I say to you.

en.L: And Saul disguised himself and put on other clothes, and he went, and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night. And he said, "Please divine for me by the spirit, and bring up for me the one whom I name to you."
en.B: So Saul disguised himself by putting on other clothes, and he set out with two men. They came to the woman at night, and he said, "Please consult the spirit for me, and bring up for me the one I name to you."
en.R: So Saul put on different clothes so that no one would know who he was. He went with two men, and they came to the woman during the night. Saul said to her, "Please use your spirit to find out the future for me. Bring up from the dead the person I name to you."

es.L: Y se disfrazó Saúl y se puso otras ropas, y fue él, y dos hombres con él, y llegaron a la mujer de noche. Y él dijo: «Adivina, te ruego, para mí por el espíritu, y hazme subir al que yo te diga».
es.B: Así que Saúl se disfrazó poniéndose otra ropa, y salió con dos hombres. Llegaron a donde estaba la mujer de noche, y él le dijo: «Por favor, consulta al espíritu por mí y hazme subir al que yo te nombre».
es.R: Así que Saúl se puso otra ropa para que nadie supiera quién era. Fue con dos hombres, y llegaron a donde estaba la mujer durante la noche. Saúl le dijo: «Por favor, usa tu espíritu para averiguar el futuro por mí. Haz subir de entre los muertos a la persona que yo te nombre».

fr.L: Et Saül se déguisa et mit d’autres vêtements, et il s’en alla, et deux hommes avec lui, et ils arrivèrent de nuit chez la femme. Et il dit : « Pratique donc pour moi la divination par l’esprit, et fais-moi monter celui que je te dirai. »
fr.B: Saül se déguisa donc en mettant d’autres vêtements, et il partit avec deux hommes. Ils arrivèrent de nuit chez la femme, et il lui dit : « Je t’en prie, consulte l’esprit pour moi et fais-moi monter celui que je vais te nommer. »
fr.R: Alors Saül a mis d’autres vêtements pour que personne ne le reconnaisse. Il est parti avec deux hommes, et ils sont arrivés chez la femme pendant la nuit. Saül lui a dit : « S’il te plaît, sers-toi de ton esprit pour connaître l’avenir pour moi. Fais monter du monde des morts la personne que je vais te nommer. »

sw.L: Sauli akajigeuza, akavaa mavazi mengine, akaenda, yeye na watu wawili pamoja naye, wakafika kwa mwanamke usiku. Akasema, "Tafadhali nibashirie kwa mzimu, unipandishie yule nitakayekutajia."
sw.B: Basi Sauli akajibadilisha kwa kuvaa mavazi mengine, akaondoka pamoja na watu wawili. Wakafika kwa yule mwanamke usiku, akamwambia, "Tafadhali uulize mzimu kwa ajili yangu, unipandishie yule nitakayekutajia."
sw.R: Basi Sauli akavaa mavazi mengine ili mtu yeyote asimtambue. Akaenda pamoja na watu wawili, wakafika kwa yule mwanamke usiku. Sauli akamwambia, "Tafadhali tumia mzimu wako unijulishe mambo yajayo. Unipandishie kutoka kwa wafu mtu nitakayekutajia."

vi.L: Sau-lơ cải trang, mặc y phục khác, rồi đi cùng hai người, và họ đến với người đàn bà ban đêm. Ông nói: "Xin bà dùng vong linh mà bói cho tôi, và gọi lên cho tôi người mà tôi sẽ nói tên với bà."
vi.B: Vậy Sau-lơ cải trang bằng cách mặc y phục khác, rồi lên đường cùng hai người. Họ đến nhà người đàn bà vào ban đêm, và ông nói: "Xin bà cầu hỏi vong linh cho tôi, và gọi lên cho tôi người mà tôi nói tên."
vi.R: Vậy Sau-lơ mặc y phục khác để không ai nhận ra mình. Ông đi cùng hai người, và họ đến nhà người đàn bà trong đêm. Sau-lơ nói với bà: "Xin bà dùng vong linh của bà mà xem điều tương lai cho tôi. Xin gọi lên từ cõi chết người mà tôi sẽ nói tên với bà."

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 변장을 하고 다른 옷을 입고, 그와 두 사람이 함께 가서, 밤에 그 여자에게 이르렀다. 그리고 그가 말했다. "부디 영으로 나를 위해 점을 쳐서, 내가 너에게 말하는 사람을 불러 올려라."
ko.B: 사울은 다른 옷을 입고 변장한 다음, 두 사람을 데리고 길을 떠났다. 그들은 밤에 그 여자에게 이르렀다. 사울이 말했다. "영에게 물어서 나를 위해 점을 쳐 다오. 내가 말하는 사람을 불러 올려라."
ko.R: 사울은 아무도 자기를 알아보지 못하게 다른 옷을 입었다. 그리고 두 사람을 데리고 밤에 그 여자를 찾아갔다. 사울이 말했다. "네가 부리는 영을 시켜 앞일을 알아봐 다오. 내가 이름을 대는 사람을 죽은 사람들 가운데서 불러 올려라."

pt.L: E Saul se disfarçou e vestiu outras roupas, e foi, ele e dois homens com ele, e chegaram à mulher de noite. E ele disse: "Adivinhe para mim, por favor, pelo espírito, e faça subir para mim aquele que eu lhe disser."
pt.B: Então Saul se disfarçou vestindo outras roupas e partiu com dois homens. Chegaram aonde a mulher estava à noite, e ele disse: "Por favor, consulte o espírito por mim e faça subir para mim aquele que eu lhe indicar."
pt.R: Então Saul vestiu outras roupas para que ninguém soubesse quem ele era. Foi com dois homens, e eles chegaram aonde a mulher estava durante a noite. Saul disse a ela: "Por favor, use o seu espírito para descobrir o futuro para mim. Faça subir dentre os mortos a pessoa que eu disser."

am.L: ሳኦልም መልኩን ለወጠ፤ ሌላም ልብስ ለበሰ፤ እርሱና ከእርሱ ጋር ሁለት ሰዎች ሄዱ፤ በሌሊትም ወደ ሴቲቱ መጡ። እርሱም፦ «እባክሽ በመንፈሱ ጠንቁዪልኝ፤ የምነግርሽንም አውጪልኝ» አላት።
am.B: ስለዚህ ሳኦል ሌላ ልብስ ለብሶ መልኩን ለወጠ፤ ከሁለት ሰዎችም ጋር ሄደ። በሌሊትም ወደ ሴቲቱ መጡ፤ እርሱም፦ «እባክሽ በመንፈሱ በኩል ጠይቂልኝ፤ የምነግርሽንም ሰው አውጪልኝ» አላት።
am.R: ስለዚህ ሳኦል ማንም እንዳያውቀው ሌላ ልብስ ለበሰ። ከሁለት ሰዎች ጋር ሄዶ በሌሊት ወደ ሴቲቱ መጡ። ሳኦልም፦ «እባክሽ በመንፈስሽ በኩል የወደፊቱን እወቂልኝ። የምነግርሽንም ሰው ከሙታን አውጪልኝ» አላት።

decisions.choice: divine for me by the spirit: seek hidden knowledge through the spirit she controls
decisions.reason: The verb is the general word for divination, forbidden to Israel in Deuteronomy 18:10. Samuel had told Saul that rebellion is like the sin of divination, using the noun of the same root (15:23). Saul now asks for the very thing.

decisions.choice: bring up: call up from below
decisions.reason: The dead were thought of as below, in the earth or in Sheol (2:6), so calling one of them was "bringing up" (verses 11, 13-15; Isaiah 29:4).

decisions.choice: he disguised himself ... by night: so as not to be known
decisions.reason: Saul hides who he is from the woman, who would fear him (verse 9), and goes at night, perhaps also to pass the Philistine camp unseen. The tall king (9:2) cannot simply be a stranger.

decisions.choice: so that no one would know who he was; use your spirit to find out the future; from the dead
decisions.reason: Readable says why Saul changed his clothes, what divining meant, and where he wanted someone brought up from.

decisions.choice: the disguised Saul and the woman say "bà", "ông" and "tôi" to each other; once she knows him she calls him "vua"
decisions.reason: Saul hides that he is king, so he speaks as an ordinary man; she changes when she sees who he is (verse 12).

decisions.choice: Saul, though disguised, speaks to the woman in the plain style (해라체); she answers in the formal polite style (합쇼체)
decisions.reason: A man used to command speaks as one; the woman, facing a stranger of rank at night, answers politely until she knows him (verse 12) and after.

decisions.choice: você (Saul to the woman)
decisions.reason: Saul speaks to the woman as a stranger to a woman of no rank, and as king to a subject, with "você" ("Adivinhe", "lhe"); she answers him with "o senhor" (verse 9), the polite address to a man of standing, before and after she knows who he is.

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּ֨ה אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֨עְתָּ֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֣ה שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִכְרִ֛ית אֶת־הָאֹב֥וֹת וְאֶת־הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֖י מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְלָמָ֥ה אַתָּ֛ה מִתְנַקֵּ֥שׁ בְּנַפְשִׁ֖י לַהֲמִיתֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the woman to him, Behold, you know what has done Saul, how he has cut off the mediums and the spiritist from the land; and why [are] you laying a snare for my life to cause me to die?

en.L: And the woman said to him, "Look, you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Then why are you laying a snare for my life, to bring about my death?"
en.B: But the woman said to him, "Surely you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Why then are you setting a trap for my life, to get me killed?"
en.R: But the woman said, "You know what Saul has done. He has gotten rid of everyone in the land who talks with the dead or with spirits. So why are you trying to trap me? Do you want me to be put to death?"

es.L: Y le dijo la mujer: «He aquí que tú sabes lo que ha hecho Saúl, cómo ha exterminado de la tierra a los médiums y a los espiritistas. ¿Por qué, pues, tiendes una trampa a mi vida para hacerme morir?».
es.B: Pero la mujer le dijo: «Tú sabes bien lo que ha hecho Saúl, cómo ha eliminado del país a los médiums y a los espiritistas. ¿Por qué, entonces, le tiendes una trampa a mi vida, para que me maten?».
es.R: Pero la mujer le dijo: «Tú sabes lo que ha hecho Saúl. Ha echado del país a todos los que hablan con los muertos o con los espíritus. Entonces, ¿por qué quieres atraparme? ¿Quieres que me condenen a muerte?».

fr.L: Et la femme lui dit : « Voici, tu sais ce qu’a fait Saül, comment il a retranché du pays les nécromanciens et les devins. Pourquoi donc tends-tu un piège à ma vie pour me faire mourir ? »
fr.B: Mais la femme lui répondit : « Tu sais bien ce qu’a fait Saül, comment il a supprimé du pays les nécromanciens et les devins. Pourquoi donc tends-tu un piège à ma vie, pour me faire tuer ? »
fr.R: Mais la femme a dit : « Tu sais ce que Saül a fait. Il s’est débarrassé de tous les gens du pays qui parlent avec les morts ou avec les esprits. Alors pourquoi est-ce que tu essaies de me piéger ? Tu veux qu’on me mette à mort ? »

sw.L: Mwanamke akamwambia, "Tazama, wewe unajua alichofanya Sauli, jinsi alivyowakatilia mbali katika nchi wanaowaita wafu na wapiga ramli. Basi kwa nini unaitegea nafsi yangu mtego, ili kunisababishia kifo?"
sw.B: Lakini mwanamke akamwambia, "Hakika unajua alichofanya Sauli, jinsi alivyowakatilia mbali katika nchi wanaowaita wafu na wapiga ramli. Kwa nini basi unanitegea mtego ili niuawe?"
sw.R: Lakini mwanamke akasema, "Unajua alichofanya Sauli. Amewaondoa katika nchi wote wanaoongea na wafu au na pepo. Basi kwa nini unajaribu kuninasa? Unataka niuawe?"

vi.L: Người đàn bà nói với ông: "Kìa, ông biết điều Sau-lơ đã làm, ông ấy đã diệt trừ các đồng cốt và thầy chiêu hồn khỏi xứ thế nào. Vậy sao ông lại gài bẫy mạng sống tôi để làm cho tôi chết?"
vi.B: Nhưng người đàn bà nói với ông: "Chắc ông biết điều Sau-lơ đã làm, ông ấy đã diệt trừ các đồng cốt và thầy chiêu hồn khỏi xứ thế nào. Vậy sao ông lại gài bẫy hại mạng tôi, để tôi bị giết?"
vi.R: Nhưng người đàn bà nói: "Ông biết điều Sau-lơ đã làm. Ông ấy đã trừ bỏ khỏi xứ tất cả những người nói chuyện với người chết hay với các vong linh. Vậy sao ông lại muốn gài bẫy tôi? Ông muốn tôi bị xử tử sao?"

ko.L: 그러자 그 여자가 그에게 말했다. "보십시오, 사울이 한 일, 곧 그가 영매들과 무당들을 이 땅에서 끊어 버린 것을 당신도 아십니다. 그런데 어찌하여 당신은 내 목숨에 올무를 놓아 나를 죽게 하려고 하십니까?"
ko.B: 그러나 그 여자가 그에게 말했다. "사울이 한 일을 당신도 아시지 않습니까? 그는 영매들과 무당들을 이 땅에서 없애 버렸습니다. 그런데 어찌하여 제 목숨에 덫을 놓아 저를 죽게 하려고 하십니까?"
ko.R: 그러나 그 여자가 말했다. "사울이 한 일을 당신도 아시지요. 그는 이 땅에서 죽은 사람이나 영들과 이야기하는 사람들을 모두 없애 버렸습니다. 그런데 왜 저를 함정에 빠뜨리려고 하십니까? 저를 죽게 하려는 것입니까?"

pt.L: E a mulher lhe disse: "Eis que o senhor sabe o que Saul fez, como eliminou da terra os médiuns e os espíritas. Por que, então, o senhor arma uma cilada para a minha vida, para me fazer morrer?"
pt.B: Mas a mulher lhe respondeu: "Certamente o senhor sabe o que Saul fez, como eliminou da terra os médiuns e os espíritas. Por que, então, o senhor está armando uma armadilha contra a minha vida, para me fazer morrer?"
pt.R: Mas a mulher disse: "O senhor sabe o que Saul fez. Ele acabou com todos no país que falam com os mortos ou com os espíritos. Então por que o senhor está tentando me pegar numa armadilha? O senhor quer que eu seja morta?"

am.L: ሴቲቱም፦ «እነሆ፣ ሳኦል ያደረገውን፣ ሙታን ጠሪዎችንና ጠንቋዮችን ከምድሪቱ እንዴት እንዳጠፋ አንተ ታውቃለህ፤ ታዲያ ልታስገድለኝ ለነፍሴ ለምን ወጥመድ ትዘረጋለህ?» አለችው።
am.B: ሴቲቱ ግን፦ «ሳኦል ያደረገውን፣ ሙታን ጠሪዎችንና ጠንቋዮችን ከምድሪቱ እንዴት እንዳጠፋ በእርግጥ ታውቃለህ። ታዲያ እንድገደል ለሕይወቴ ለምን ወጥመድ ትዘረጋለህ?» አለችው።
am.R: ሴቲቱ ግን፦ «ሳኦል ያደረገውን ታውቃለህ። ከሙታን ወይም ከመናፍስት ጋር የሚነጋገሩትን ሁሉ ከምድሪቱ አስወግዷል። ታዲያ ለምን ልታጠምደኝ ትፈልጋለህ? እንድገደል ትፈልጋለህን?» አለችው።

decisions.choice: cut off: removed, perhaps by putting them to death
decisions.reason: Verse 3 says Saul "removed" them. "Cut off" can mean to drive out or to destroy, and the law set death as the penalty (Leviticus 20:27). The text does not say which Saul did; the woman fears for her life either way.

decisions.choice: laying a snare for my life: trying to trap me into a crime that carries death
decisions.reason: She suspects that the stranger is an informer or a trap set by the king.

decisions.choice: you know what Saul has done: she speaks of Saul to Saul
decisions.reason: The woman does not know she is talking to the king. The reader does, and hears the irony.

decisions.choice: the spiritists: one word used for the whole group
decisions.reason: The second word is singular here, unlike verse 3, but it names the whole class of such people.

decisions.choice: Do you want me to be put to death?
decisions.reason: Readable splits the question in two, and describes the mediums and spiritists as in verse 3.

decisions.choice: eliminou
decisions.reason: "Eliminar" keeps both senses of "cut off" that m1 leaves open, driving out and putting to death; "cortar" does not say this of people in Portuguese, and "matar" would choose one sense.

decisions.choice: the woman says "አንተ" to the stranger (verses 9-12) and "እርስዎ" to the king once she knows him (verses 21-22); Saul says "አንቺ" to her
decisions.reason: Saul has disguised himself (verse 8), so she speaks to an unknown man at night; after she learns that he is the king (verse 12) she calls herself "your maidservant" (verse 21, meaning decision m2 there), the courtly form, and Amharic changes with her.

decisions.choice: as the LORD lives, if punishment befalls you: an oath meaning "it will not befall you"
decisions.reason: In a Hebrew oath, "if" with the rest of a curse left unsaid means "certainly not": "may God deal with me if it happens". So Saul swears that she will not be punished (14:45; 19:6).

decisions.choice: Saul swears by the LORD: he calls on the LORD to protect what the LORD's law forbids
decisions.reason: The LORD had not answered Saul (verse 6), yet he uses the LORD's name to promise safety for consulting the dead, which the law punishes (Leviticus 20:6, 27). The king who enforced the law now promises to set it aside.

decisions.choice: punishment: guilt and the penalty it brings
decisions.reason: The word can mean the wrong itself, the guilt for it, or its punishment (Genesis 4:13). With "befall you" it means the penalty.

decisions.choice: made a promise to her in the name of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable explains "swore by the LORD" as a promise made in his name.

decisions.choice: Tão certo como o SENHOR vive
decisions.reason: The oath takes the book's form of 19:6 in Portuguese, with the words the Hebrew leaves understood in brackets at Literal; every level gives the sense of the "if" clause as a promise that nothing will befall her (m1), as the English does.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew oath "if punishment befalls you" is said as a plain negative
decisions.reason: Amharic has no oath form with a bare "if"; as meaning decision m1 says, the oath means "it will not befall you", and every level says so.

decisions.choice: the woman saw Samuel: the narrator presents the figure as Samuel himself
alternatives: a spirit that only appeared to be Samuel
decisions.reason: From here on the narrator calls the one who appears "Samuel" (verses 12, 14, 15, 16, 20), not a spirit or an appearance of him. He speaks as Samuel spoke, repeats Samuel's own words of 15:28, and says what will happen, and it does happen (31:1-6). The woman's terrified cry may show that this was not what she expected from her practice. The text does not explain how it happened, and it never says that her arts had power to bring up the dead; the plainest reading is that God allowed Samuel to come and speak one last word of judgment. Others have read it as a spirit pretending to be Samuel, or as a trick by the woman; the narrator gives no hint of either. Nothing here approves of consulting the dead, which this book and the law condemn (verse 3; 1 Chronicles 10:13).

decisions.choice: you are Saul: she now knows who he is
decisions.reason: The text does not say how she knew. It may be that only the king would ask for Samuel, or that the appearance itself made it plain.

decisions.choice: deceived me: tricked me
decisions.reason: Saul had hidden who he was (verse 8). Now she fears that the king who banned her trade has caught her at it.

decisions.choice: screamed
decisions.reason: "Cried out with a loud voice" is a scream of terror, and Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: "ሳሙኤልን ባየች ጊዜ": the figure is named Samuel, with no word for a spirit or an appearance
decisions.reason: Meaning decision m1: the narrator calls the one who appears "Samuel" from here on, and the Amharic does the same at every level.
